_comment: Properly translucent, leaning on the compositor's blur to stay readable. The built-in look sits at 0.975 on cards because it must survive a compositor that does not blur at all; this one assumes blur is on and trades that safety for actual glass. If text behind the card becomes readable, your compositor is not blurring — use glass-dark instead.
_alpha: Cards drop from 0.975 to 0.72 — the single change that makes blur visible at all. The panel and OSD follow.
_content: Rows stay noticeably more solid than the sheet they sit on. Translucent content over translucent glass is where legibility actually breaks.
_edge: A brighter lit edge than the default: at low alpha the surface loses its boundary and stops reading as a distinct sheet.
_blur: Saturation carries the material. At 1.0 a translucent surface reads as grey haze; the chroma coming through is what makes it look like glass rather than fog.
_depth: A wider, softer shadow: at low alpha the surface needs the shadow to separate it from the desktop, because the fill no longer does it.
